newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates rise ahead of the weekend.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates rise ahead of the weekend.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were bidding higher on Friday, with dealers noting that the rise was not prompted by yesterday's rate hike.
They said it was mainly a matter of distribution of liquidity among participants ahead of the weekend.
Call money was bid at around 3.18 percent in afternoon trade versus 3.00 percent bid earlier and 2.88 percent before Thursday's rate hike.
The Dutch central bank raised the special advances rate by 10 basis points to 3.00 percent yesterday to support the guilder versus the German mark.
The guilder was a touch stronger versus the mark at 112.5875 per 100 marks compared to 112.60 before the rise of the special advances rate.
Deposits up to three months were fractionally higher.
Three-month deposits were bid two basis points higher at 3.14 percent.
